## Connecting to the database

``` r
library(renmods)
library(lubridate)
```


Download/update the data and save to your cache.


``` r
renmods_update(datasets = "all")
```


Connect to the database EnMoDS table


``` r
db <- renmods_connect()
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr", "yr_2_5", "yr_5_10", and "historic" data
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_2_5: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:34:36 (within 26 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_5_10: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:35:55 (within 26 week(s))
#> ✔ historic: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:39:04 (within 26 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
```

Optionally, prefilter by dataset or date range.


``` r
db <- renmods_connect(datasets = "this_yr")
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr" data
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
db <- renmods_connect(dates = c("2024-12-15", "2025-01-15"))
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr" and "yr_2_5" data for dates between 2024-12-15 and 2025-01-15
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_2_5: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:34:36 (within 26 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
db <- renmods_connect(dates = c("2026-01-01", "2026-01-31"))
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr" data for dates between 2026-01-01 and 2026-01-31
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
```


## Collecting data into memory

Collect the data into a data frame (from a database connection) for working/saving.
The smaller the data set and the fewer datasets, the faster this will go.
However, because we use Parquet files to store the data, this is pretty fast to
start.


``` r
df <- collect(db)
```

Or use the dplyr package to do more filtering before you collect the data.


``` r
library(dplyr)
```

## Dates and Times

EnMoDS stores date/times as character/text fields with the timezone indicated by +/- offset (e.g., '-08:00'). However, in R all values in a column must use the same timezone. Therefore renmods converts times to UTC-7:00
(called `Etc/GMT+7`, note that `+` is correct; see the [Wikipedia page on
timezones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones#List)).

This may not be always ideal depending on the region you're working in, so 
the original timezone from `Observed_Date_Time` is stored in a new field `ren_tz`
for reference. You can convert to any timezone using the [lubridate::with_tz()](https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/reference/with_tz.html) function.

We can see that we're in UTC -7 by looking at the first couple of values.

``` r
df$Observed_Date_Time[1:5]
#> [1] "2026-01-05 15:35:00 -07" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 -07" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 -07"
#> [4] "2026-01-05 15:35:00 -07" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 -07"
```

If we want to be in UTC -6:00 we can convert with lubridate's `with_tz()` function.


``` r
with_tz(df$Observed_Date_Time[1:5], tz = "Etc/GMT+6")
#> [1] "2026-01-05 16:35:00 -06" "2026-01-05 16:35:00 -06" "2026-01-05 16:35:00 -06"
#> [4] "2026-01-05 16:35:00 -06" "2026-01-05 16:35:00 -06"
```

This only converts the first 5 observations, just for illustration.

If we want to convert the entire data frame to Mountain time (including DST depending on the time of year),
we could use the `America/Edmonton` timezone.


``` r
df_tz <- mutate(
  df,
  Observed_Date_Time = with_tz(Observed_Date_Time, "America/Edmonton")
)
# Take a look:
df_tz$Observed_Date_Time[1:5]
#> [1] "2026-01-05 15:35:00 MST" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 MST" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 MST"
#> [4] "2026-01-05 15:35:00 MST" "2026-01-05 15:35:00 MST"
```

If you wanted to convert all time columns at once, you could use the `across()`
function from dplyr.

First we'll get the whole data set again

``` r
df <- renmods_connect(dates = c("2024-12-15", "2025-01-15")) |>
  collect()
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr" and "yr_2_5" data for dates between 2024-12-15 and 2025-01-15
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_2_5: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:34:36 (within 26 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
```

What time columns do we have?

``` r
select(df, contains("Time"))
#> # A tibble: 127,902 × 8
#>    Field_Visit_Start_Time Field_Visit_End_Time Observed_Date_Time  Observed_Date_Time_Start
#>    <dttm>                 <dttm>               <dttm>              <dttm>

#>  4 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00

#>  6 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00     
#>  7 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00     
#>  8 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00     
#>  9 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00     
#> 10 2025-01-06 10:00:00    NA                   2025-01-06 10:00:00 2025-01-06 10:00:00

#> #   Lab_Arrival_Date_Time <dttm>, Lab_Prepared_Date_Time <dttm>
```

We can use the tidyselector `contains()` with across to apply a function *across* a series of columns.

``` r
df_tz <- mutate(
  df,
  across(contains("Time"), \(col) with_tz(col, "America/Edmonton"))
)

# Take a look:
df_tz$Observed_Date_Time[1:5]
#> [1] "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST"
#> [4] "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST"
df_tz$Field_Visit_Start_Time[1:5]
#> [1] "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST"
#> [4] "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST" "2025-01-06 10:00:00 MST"
```

Finally, you can also prevent any date/time conversion and leave those fields
as character.


``` r
df <- renmods_connect(
  dates = c("2024-12-15", "2025-01-15"),
  convert_times = FALSE
) |>
  collect()
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr" and "yr_2_5" data for dates between 2024-12-15 and 2025-01-15

#> ✔ yr_2_5: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:34:36 (within 26 week(s))

#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

# Note columns are character now
select(df, contains("Time"))
```

## Different Result Types

By default, renmods returns only observations with a Numeric result value. 
However, you can return non-numeric values with the `result_type` argument.


``` r
df <- renmods_connect(result_type = "non-numeric") |>
  filter(Location_ID == "DS8802967") |>
  collect()
#> ℹ Connecting to "this_yr", "yr_2_5", "yr_5_10", and "historic" data
#> ✔ this_yr: Last downloaded 2026-11-12 14:51:07 (within 1 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_2_5: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:34:36 (within 26 week(s))
#> ✔ yr_5_10: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:35:55 (within 26 week(s))
#> ✔ historic: Last downloaded 2026-11-10 16:39:04 (within 26 week(s))
#> duckdb is storing downloaded extensions and secrets under ~/.duckdb:
#> ℹ /home/steffi/.duckdb
#> This persists across sessions and is shared with the DuckDB CLI and other clients.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to use a temporary directory instead.
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
df |> select(Observed_Property_ID, Result_Value, Observed_Property_Result_Type)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   Observed_Property_ID                          Result_Value Observed_Property_Result_Type
#>   <chr>                                         <chr>        <chr>                        
#> 1 PHCs F4 Reached Baseline at nC50 (True/False) True         CATEGORICAL_FIXED_VALUES
```

You can also return *both* numeric and non-numeric result values with `result_type = 'all'`, but we advise against that as the `Result_Value` column will be a character (text) column, so even numeric values will be considered. 
If you need both, we recommend collecting each separately, and then combining them in a way that makes sense for your work.


## Disconnecting

Don't forget to close the connection to the database


``` r
renmods_disconnect(db)
```
